name: Shared Storage — Cross-Node Concurrent Writer Rotation Converges
description:
Belt-and-suspenders integration coverage for the convergence guarantee of a cell's writer set. The set is the fold of the cell's governance rotation ops (`shared_writers::fold`), which reads only the ops and their causal pasts, so it is total and symmetric across nodes. That is covered by unit/node tests; the one angle not exercised there is a genuinely-concurrent, multi-node rotation that has to converge end-to-end over real sync. This workflow is that test.
Identities (each held by exactly one node, so each can actually execute writes and have them accepted/rejected):
  * A = node-1
  * B = node-2
  * C = node-3

Making the two rotations DAG-concurrent --------------------------------------- node-1 and node-2 must each rotate from the same head H without having seen the other's rotation. We use merobox's `partition_peers` / `heal_peers` steps (merobox#278), which drop ONLY libp2p traffic between the named peers while leaving every node RPC-reachable — so we can drive BOTH rotators while they are partitioned, with no window-juggling:

  1. partition_peers node-1 from {node-2, node-3}. node-1 is now
     libp2p-isolated from BOTH (so node-3 can't relay node-2's
     rotation to node-1) yet all three stay callable.
  2. node-1 rotates {A,B} -> {A,C} (drops B, adds C). node-2 rotates
     {A,B} -> {A} (drops B, itself). Neither can see the other's
     rotation, so they are causally CONCURRENT from head H.
  3. heal_peers, then wait_for_sync converges all three — the
     root-hash convergence assertion — with both rotations merged.
  4. Assert every node resolves the SAME writer set directly from
     the two concurrent rotations — no settling rotation needed
     (see the note below). Both rotations dropped B and kept
     A, so the resolved set retains A and revokes B on every node —
     retroactive revocation of a baseline writer under concurrency.
     B's own step is void (node-1's concurrent step removes B's
     ADMIN), so {A, C} applies on every node.
  5. Assert the rotated-out writer's write is rejected: node-2 (B)
     calling `shared_set` fails on every node, while node-1 (A)
     writing succeeds and the legitimate value converges.

Why no settling rotation: the fold depends on the rotation ops and their causal pasts, never on the order a node received them, so every node resolves the SAME set straight from the two concurrent rotations. This workflow originally issued a causally-latest "settling" rotation by node-3 because the writer set then read from per-node insertion order.
The two rotations ({A,C} from node-1, {A} from node-2) deliberately DIFFER, yet BOTH drop B and keep A. Every writer holds ADMIN, and node-1's step removes B's ADMIN, so node-2's step (authored by B) is void and the fold applies {A, C} deterministically: A and C are writers and B is revoked on all three nodes. The post-heal `wait_for_sync` asserts storage-root convergence.
Why a plain bridge (no NAT): the concurrent-rotation guarantee is a CRDT/merge property — it has nothing to do with relay recovery, which is the whole point of the NAT topology the sync-resilience partition workflows use. `partition_peers` drops the peers' libp2p packets at the host's DOCKER-USER iptables chain (matched on the containers' bridge IPs), so it is a clean, RPC-preserving libp2p cut on a plain bridge — and heal re-establishes direct connections quickly, with no relay-reservation re-registration to wait on.
Belt-and-suspenders: if the two rotations ever turn out NOT to be concurrent (e.g. a partition leak), they reconcile causally and the convergence assertions still hold — the worst case is weaker coverage or a failing C assertion, never a false pass. The fully-deterministic guarantee lives in the fold's unit tests (crates/storage/src/shared_writers.rs); this is the real-network layer on top.
